name: Izar
description: A naked-eye star 72.3 parsecs away, 37.6 times the Sun's width: its disc was measured with the Navy Precision Optical Interferometer.

radius.source: Baines et al. (2021), AJ 162, 198, HD 129989: radius 37.61 +1.29/-1.38 solar radii (Table 5), from the limb-darkened angular diameter 4.84 +/- 0.01 mas (NPOI, Table 4) and the Gaia EDR3 (Gaia Collaboration 2021) parallax

temperature.source: Baines et al. (2021), AJ 162, 198, HD 129989: effective temperature 4755 +/- 66 K (Table 5), from the angular diameter and the bolometric flux of the SED fit

gravity.source: Baines et al. (2021), AJ 162, 198, HD 129989: log g 2.24, from Soubiran et al. (2016), PASTEL, as the paper lists it beside the diameter (Table 4)

distance.source: Baines et al. (2021), AJ 162, 198, HD 129989: the Gaia EDR3 (Gaia Collaboration 2021) parallax the radius was computed with (Table 1), 13.83 +/- 0.49 mas, inverted

text.card: A naked-eye star 72 parsecs away whose disc the NPOI measured: 37.6 times the Sun's width.
text.introduction: Its disc spans 4.84 milliarcseconds, which gives 37.61 solar radii and 4,755 K at its surface.
text.locator: Tables 1, 4 and 5, HD 129989: parallax, limb-darkened diameter, radius, Teff

radialVelocity.source: SIMBAD's radial velocity for Gaia DR3 1279798794197267072 (quality A), from 1979IAUS...30...57E; Gaia DR3 measures none
